entries.answer: An atom is the smallest unit of ordinary matter that keeps an element's properties, made of a nucleus of protons and neutrons surrounded by electrons. The number of protons is the atomic number and it alone defines which element it is, so changing it changes the element. The electrons determine the chemistry, and the electron shells filling in a particular pattern is the whole reason the periodic table has a shape.

patterns: how is the periodic table organised
entries.answer: The periodic table arranges the elements by atomic number, which puts elements with similar electron structures into the same column. That is why it works as a predictor rather than a list, because an element's position tells you how it will react and the group number gives the valence electrons. The table has no gaps and no exceptions, which is a stronger claim about physics than it looks.

entries.answer: Atoms bond because being bonded is a lower energy state than being separate, and the type of bond is decided by how the electrons are shared or transferred. Covalent bonds share electron pairs and produce the familiar molecules, ionic bonds are a transfer that leaves charged ions, and metallic bonds are a shared sea of electrons holding a lattice together. Bond type predicts properties well, which is why it is taught before any reaction.
